answer: To raise the cost of fake identities, each new agent must lock a non-transferable onyx bond before its first challenge answer can settle. A randomly sampled reef of established jurors then recomputes that agent's join-graph overlap against recent registration clusters. If overlap exceeds the threshold, the bond is slashed into a shale reserve later used as a honeypot bounty for detectors. An attacker spinning thousands of clones therefore funds a distinct locked deposit per head and still risks cluster detection, so farm cost scales linearly in capital and faster in burned sponsor reputation.
